citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
- There is a bottle of expired medication in the kennel which the licensee was using to treat puppies. Expired medications
can have unpredictable effects and are not an appropriate method of veterinary care. All expired medications should be
discarded.
Correct from this date (14 October 2026) forward.

citations.desc: Records: Operators of auction sales and brokers.
citations.narrative:
- The facility had five puppies on hand and could not provide proper acquisition records for all five animals. Brokers must
keep records which disclose all required information for each puppy purchased by the facility. These records must be kept
by the facility and made available to USDA inspectors as requested.
Correct from this date (14 October 2026) forward

- The facility contingency plan does not adequately account for reasonably foreseeable situations that might impact the
licensee. There are no considerations for potential weather impacts to the home facility, and no consideration for
problems that might arise while transporting puppies. Contingency plans must identify situations the licensee might
experience that would trigger the need for the measures identified in a contingency plan to be put into action. The
licensee must modify their contingency plan and keep it updated as needed.
Correct by 22 October 2026

-There are multiple bottles of toxic materials not being stored in cabinets in housing areas of the puppy building. An open
bucket containing a mix of sanitizers is stored on the floor directly next to puppy enclosures and food storage containers.
If spilled, improperly stored toxins such as cleaning and sanitizing supplies can contaminate items in the area, in this case
dog food. Spilled cleaning supplies can also be an ocular or respiratory irritant to the exposed animals. The licensee must
ensure that all substances that are toxic to dogs but are required for normal husbandry, are stored in cabinets if they are
stored in animal housing or food storage and preparation areas.
Correct by 22 October 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
- Multiple hard plastic food and water bowls are excessively damaged, scratched, and chewed. These bowls have
reached a point where they are so worn, they cannot be properly cleaned and sanitized. Failure to properly clean and
sanitize food and water bowls can have a negative impact on the health of the enclosed puppies. The facility must either
replace the existing bowls with appropriate receptacles, or repair the surface damage of the existing bowls.
Correct by: 22 October 2026
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class “B” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by 14 December 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
You may appeal this finding in writing by (insert date which is 7 days after issuance of report).
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
